newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico 1997 net spending to rise 5.2 pct - gov't.
newsitem.headline: Mexico 1997 net spending to rise 5.2 pct - gov't.

text.p: Mexico's 1997 budget sees total net spending of 725.79 billion pesos, an increase of 5.2 percent from the year before, and nine percent real growth in social spending, the finance ministry said Thursday.

"In 1997 total net spending -- total spending in the public sector less debt amortizations -- will increase in real terms by 5.2 percent compared to expected 1996 spending," the ministry said in the budget proposal it handed to Congress on Thursday.
Finance Minister Guillermo Ortiz told deputies that, "social spending in 1997 will grow nine percent in real terms."
The government also said planned government spending in 1997 will equal 506.69 billion pesos, up 4.1 percent from 1996 levels.
Social spending will equal 55.8 percent of total planned spending, according to the federal government's 1997 budget.
